A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Plugin research and include readable main text and Appendices A–C. Methods, equations, proofs, experiments, and figures can be matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments across four datasets, architectural ablations, distribution-shift analyses, and a human evaluation of 100 Adidas samples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds TempNet, BDPL, and LoRA comparisons, computational-cost results, and domain-vocabulary measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Algorithm 1 retain normalized multiplication of base-model and reweighting probabilities, training only the reweighting model, and greedy inference. The BDPL wrapper applies this existing procedure using an optimized prompt; no new Plugin component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions use E2E NLG, Web NLG, CommonGen, and Adidas, including the same infrastructure/person and man/woman distribution shifts. The added comparisons reuse this coverage. Calling the Adidas setting an extreme distribution shift does not introduce a new test scenario.

E2.justification: v3 adds TempNet across all three base models and four datasets in Tables 1–4, BDPL with and without Plugin using GPT2-XL in Table 5, and rank-8 LoRA using GPT2-XL and LLaMA-3.1-8B in Table 7. The original comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: Existing splits, 40% hyper-validation allocation, training settings, seven generation metrics, and greedy decoding are retained. Added protocols include a 75-call BDPL optimization budget, rank-8 LoRA on query/value projections, FLOP comparisons for up to 64 decoding steps, and an Adidas domain-term occurrence measure.

E4.justification: v3 adds a comparison isolating Plugin's benefit with BDPL-optimized prompts, a parameter/FLOP analysis against LoRA, and quantitative Adidas vocabulary analysis. Existing base-quality, depth, architecture, distribution-shift, and human-evaluation analyses remain intact.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting; v3 follows that convention for TempNet and LoRA. No increased run count or new statistical estimation procedure is stated. The added BDPL table supplies only point estimates.

E6.justification: All 72 original benchmark rows are unchanged. v3 adds TempNet, BDPL/composition, LoRA, and efficiency results. LoRA has higher mean BLEU than Plugin in all eight Table 7 settings; Table 5 reports gains from combining BDPL and Plugin. Adidas term rates of 25.6% versus 13.8% are new. The text also replaces Figure 4's step-51/ambition account with step-59/recycled, although the figure retains the former.

T1.justification: The loss-correction derivation, Assumptions 5.1–5.2 and B.1, Theorem 1, and Appendix B's lemmas and proofs are retained. The added finite-time novelty sentence in Section 5 introduces no new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the claims about logit-based adaptation, label-noise correction, consistency guarantees, and empirical effectiveness. The additional comparisons support the existing contribution without redefining it.

C2.justification: v3 characterizes retained shifts as partly adversarial or extreme, explains vocabulary-preserving soft reweighting, and discusses compatibility with prompt learning and competitiveness with LoRA. It removes v1 Appendix C.4's explanation that noisy GPT2-M predictions favor NewModel on E2E NLG. The reasoning and computational-overhead limitations remain.

D1.justification: New details include LoRA's rank and target projections, BDPL's call budget, and the efficiency comparison: 30.72M versus 2.46M parameters and 196.2B versus 188.8B FLOPs for Plugin versus LoRA. Existing prompts, hyperparameter information, and code-access link remain. TempNet and BDPL source citations are unresolved.

R1.justification: v3 removes the Narasimhan et al. (2014) reference, adds discussion of gradient/adapter equivalence, and expands positioning relative to TempNet, BDPL, and white-box PEFT. The broader related-work framework remains stable. Several added citations render as question marks, leaving their intended sources unidentified.

P1.justification: There are localized prose revisions, including the theory summary, Impact Statement, and appendix analysis. Experiments gain a wrapper subsection, and Appendix C.4 is repurposed after relocating GPT2-M results. Affiliations and correspondence information change, and acknowledgements are added; the overall narrative order remains stable.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper in the main text, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. GPT2-M results from v1 Tables 6–9 are merged into v3 Tables 1–4, and new BDPL and LoRA tables are added. All eight underlying figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The BDPL and LoRA comparisons and efficiency analysis add useful context absent from v1, while preserving the original method, proofs, and scores. However, unresolved baseline citations, missing BDPL uncertainty, and the new Figure 4 text mismatch weaken the additions. TempNet's description also leaves unexplained how uniform temperature scaling produces different outputs under the stated greedy decoding. These unresolved evidential problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
